note: How he takes it and how he goes down, cut from the 143-frame ASSETS/SeniorAgberoReactionFall.png rather than the older 77-frame NEW SPRITES export. TWO takes, not one: the recoil is 0-53 (guard, fold, driven back, hard cut at 54) and the knockdown is 54-142 (guard, load, air, crash, get up). THE STANDING TIERS SHARE ONE CLIP: `heavyHit` is 0-35 and a light hit is the same art cut short by its own timer, so the two can never disagree about where he is standing. THE HELD BEAT-DOWN HAS ITS OWN: `hardHit` is the artist's 36-53 section — short enough to fit between two punches, because it RESTARTS on every one of them, and it opens already folded for the same reason.

sections.name: Heavy Hit
sections.description: The recoil, EVERY frame of it at the source rate — 36 poses in 1.2s, a new one every 33ms. It shipped as every-second-frame at 24fps and that was a visible stutter on a man who is supposed to feel heavy. He keeps his feet the whole way (foot line never leaves 561-571), so this is a stagger, not a knockdown. Both STANDING hit tiers play this clip; the light one is cut short by its own timer rather than by having its own art. NOTE frames 0-11: they are within 6 source px of the guard pose (2.4 px at the drawn scale), i.e. invisible. That is fine for a standing stagger, which runs 0.38-0.86s and gets well past them — it is NOT fine for a grab beat-down, which is why `hardHit` below exists.

sections.name: Hard Hit
sections.description: The reaction he plays while HELD and being beaten, RESTARTED ON EVERY BLOW so a six-punch beat-down reads as six reactions. 18 frames, 0.60s — deliberately a little longer than the 0.32-0.38s between strikes, so each punch shows most of it (36 out to about 46, x1 614 -> 674) and a wider gap runs it all the way to 53 at x1 746. Every frame of the artist's own 36+ section, at the source rate. It opens ALREADY FOLDED because it restarts: a clip that builds from the guard pose can only ever show its build-up when it is re-triggered every third of a second, which is what made the previous 0-35 cut look like no reaction at all.

sections.name: Fall Air
sections.description: Off his feet. The foot line is the tell and it is unambiguous: he is planted through 80 (foot 568), then 554, 530, 510, 492, 474, 448, 418, 388 and 362 — genuinely airborne — before coming back down through 422, 478, 516 and 550 at 102, one frame short of settling. Starts at 81 because that is the first frame his feet leave the road; 74-80 is the load, and opening a knockdown on seven grounded frames reads as lag. THE APEX TUCK (92-95) IS DELIBERATELY OMITTED — see the comment above; it is the only intentional frame drop on these sheets and it exists because those four poses are half his standing height and made a bigger man read as a smaller one.

sections.name: Fall Down
sections.description: Down. Foot line settles at 558-560 and the ink box goes wide and flat (y0 344-348, width 622-642) — he is prone on the tarmac. Holds its last frame for however long the down timer runs, which is why it is short.

sections.name: Death Down
sections.description: The last thing he does. Ends ON FRAME 106 and holds it — the requested death pose. Shares 103-105 with fallDown so the crash into it is the same performance; only where it STOPS differs, which is the whole distinction between a knockdown and a killing blow.

sections.name: Get Up
sections.description: Back onto his feet, and it lands where it has to: frame 142 measures y0 22 / foot 562 / width 416 against the guard pose at y0 24 / foot 568 / width 424 — within six pixels on every axis. He stands up INTO the stance the walk and attack sheets expect, so the handover out of a knockdown never pops. 32 frames against the old export's 13, which is why the recovery no longer snaps.
